 KEY MATCH DETAILS: (India A vs. Nepal ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars)

 Captains:  Tilak Varma ( India ), Sandeep Lamichhane (Nepal)

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement India A vs. Nepal ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars Live Score & Updates
 Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the India vs. Nepal ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha. 
 After 40 overs, India are 221/3 
 India A piled on 92 runs without losing a wicket from overs 31 to 40.
 Kushagra reached his hundred to sit unbeaten on 101* off 94 balls (8x4, 4x6, SR: 107.44), after accelerating rapidly following his half-century.
 Captain Tilak Varma matched the tempo at the other end, reaching 76* off 94 balls (3x4, 3x6, SR: 80.85) as the pair stretched their unbroken fourth-wicket stand to 179 runs.
 After 30 overs, India are 129/3 
 India A added 55 runs without losing a wicket across overs 21 to 30. 
 After coming together at 42/3 in the 11th over, Kumar Kushagra and Tilak Varma completely neutralised Nepal's middle-overs attack.
 Kushagra led the counterattack to reach 48* off 54 balls (4x4, 1x6). While, Varma provided steady support at the other end, reaching 42* off 74 balls (2x4) to keep the innings on track.
 After 20 overs, India A are 74/3 
 India A struggled to break free against Nepal's spin-heavy middle-overs squeeze and could add just 32 runs in the next 10 overs. 
 Pawan Sarraf struck on the third ball of the 11th over (10.3 ov), bowling opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 26 off 32 balls (3x4, 1x6) to leave India A at 42/3.
 Captain Tilak Varma (19* off 45 balls) and wicketkeeper Kumar Kushagra (16* off 23 balls, 1x4) compiled an unbroken 32-run fourth-wicket stand to arrest the slide, striking just one boundary across the 10-over phase.
 After 10 overs, India A are 42/2 
 Nandan Yadav removed Abhishek Sharma (9 off 13, 1x6) on the first ball of the 6th over (29/1), before left-arm spinner Lalit Rajbanshi had Ayush Badoni stumped for 2 in his very first over (36/2, 6.6 ov).
 Opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi held firm at one end to reach 26* off 29 balls (3x4, 1x6), batting alongside captain Tilak Varma (3* off 11 balls) at the close of the first Powerplay.
 Toss result: 
 Nepal won the toss and elected to bowl first.
